subject: Nimbus Health — cost discovery & target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@cortexlabs.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus Health — cost discovery & target $/1M tokens

Hi Alex, Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed: 

Summary from call
- Baseline expected token consumption: ~30M tokens/month (inference tokens across text generation flows).
- Peak traffic: up to ~90M tokens in promotional spikes (3x baseline) for specific campaigns.
- Model profile: mostly medium-length responses (average generation ~450 tokens), a mix of retrieval-augmented prompts and chat-style completion.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is a must; they also want data residency options in US regions.

Commercial signals
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting parity with your current host and expressed a target band of roughly $8–$12 per 1M tokens, with $9/1M being the ideal go-to number to evaluate.
- Procurement cadence: small pilot first (4–6 weeks), then an evaluation to decide on a reserved commit if performance + cost look good.

How Redwood can help (quick points)
- We can get to competitive effective $/1M through a combination of continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, and model-variant routing.
- For pilots we propose hosted inference to move quickly; Dedicated pools are available for predictable throughput if they want committed discounts.

Attachments: I've included a first-pass PoC cost estimate for the baseline and spike scenarios (Nimbus_PoC_cost_estimate_v1.xlsx). It contains line-item assumptions (tokens/session, concurrency, cache hit estimates).

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm baseline tokens/month and expected percent of traffic that needs <200ms p99 latency vs relaxed latency (we used 30% low-latency in the attached estimate)?
2) Confirm whether SOC 2 + US residency is required for pilot or only for production.
3) We'll prepare a short competitive parity table (Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs current host + OpenAI/Anthropic) and a 4-week pilot scope by Friday.

If that sounds right, we'll schedule a quick internal pricing sync and send a calendar invite for a demo next week.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Nimbus Health — cost discovery & target $/1M tokens

Thanks Karthik — this is perfect and matches our notes. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline is ~30M tokens/month (confirmed). Peak up to ~85–95M (mostly daytime promotional loads).
- Latency split: roughly 25% p99 <200ms (real-time chat), remainder is fine with 500–800ms.
- Compliance: We need SOC 2 for pilot data access (security team will audit logs).
- Target pricing: we are trying to move from our current host at roughly $18–20/1M down to a practical target near $9/1M. If Redwood can present an anchored comparison that shows $9 effective for our workload (considering caching and batching), procurement is likely to endorse pilot spend.

Can you share the parity table and any examples of similar customers who moved from OpenAI/Anthropic to Redwood with unit-cost improvements? Also, is there a simple way for us to estimate effective unit price after prefix/KV caching?

I'll review the PoC estimate this afternoon and loop in our procurement lead if numbers look reasonable.

- Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering
Cortex Labs (technical contact for Nimbus pilot)
alex@cortexlabs.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nimbus Health — cost discovery & target $/1M tokens

Forwarding Alex's reply — sounds like a realistic opportunity. Internal notes / suggested approach: 

1) Pricing parity table (owner: Marissa) — build a concise 1-page table with expected effective $/1M for the Nimbus workload across: Redwood Hosted (pilot), Redwood Dedicated (committed), OpenAI hosted, Anthropic hosted, and a representative open-host (e.g., GPU VPS + quantized model). Use the following starter assumptions (we'll refine):
   - Redwood Hosted (pilot): $9/1M (effective) assuming 35% cache hit and batching improvements on median throughput.
   - Redwood Dedicated (12-mo commit): $7/1M (effective) with reserved GPU pools and quantization profiles.
   - OpenAI (equivalent model): $18/1M (list host price for current gen model).
   - Anthropic (equivalent model): $16/1M.
   - Open-host reference (self-hosted quantized on cloud): $6–10/1M but with higher ops burden and unpredictable tail latency.

2) Pilot scope (owner: Karthik) — 4 weeks, 2 endpoints, 1 parallel integration engineer from their side, SOC 2 evidence packet shared. Goals: validate effective $/1M at baseline, p99 latency for real-time flows, and cache hit ratios. Deliverable: a one-page unit-econ summary after 4 weeks.

3) Assets to attach — I've uploaded a starter CSV with simple parity numbers (token-parity-benchmarks.csv). Marissa, please create the 1-page parity slide and a short procurement note they can use to justify pilot spend (showing potential annualized savings).

4) Pricing ask — if they accept pilot assumptions we can quote a pilot rate (hosted) of $9/1M with a credit to offset onboarding. If they go Dedicated with a 12-month commit we should propose $7/1M. Keep the open-host numbers as context but emphasize Redwood's SLA and operational benefits.

Lmk if you want me to jump on a call with procurement.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
